name: Policymakers back expert group's initiative on SDGs

content.title: Policymakers back expert group's initiative on SDGs
content.summary: Stakeholders from all sectors to work together to achieve targets on health-related SDGs.

media.caption: Federal Minister for Planning, Development and Reform Ahsan Iqbal and Minister of State for National Health Services, Regulation and Coordination Saira Afzal Tarar listen to proposals at the conference.
media.alt: Policymakers back expert group's initiative on SDGs
Policymakers back expert group's initiative on SDGs

content.text: A multi-stakeholder autonomous committee of parliamentarians, public health experts, researchers and civil society representatives will be set up to develop a road map to achieve the health-related Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)

Minister of State for Health Saira Afzal Tarar announced the formation of the committee, known as the Joint Health SDG Committee, at the conclusion of a two-day workshop in Islamabad jointly organised by Aga Khan University, the Federal Ministry of Health Services and Regulation, the World Health Organization (WHO), and the Pakistan Academy of Sciences.
In her speech at the event, Mrs Tarar explained that achieving the targets of SDG 3
Ensure healthy lives and promote wellbeing for all at all ages
- the economic, social, environmental and behavioural factors that influence an individual's wellbeing.

She noted that while the country's National Health Vision 2016-2025 has already incorporated targets under the SDGs, the Joint Health SDGs Committee could play an important, complementary role in achieving the country's healthcare objectives.

In her keynote speech at the event, the minister stated: "I endorse the formation of Joint Health SDG Committee ... this group will identify gaps and develop priority, costed action plans to fill these gaps, which will be in line with National Health Vision 2025.

"We also endorse the need to develop monitoring and accountability mechanisms to get required outcomes, and [it is the] responsibility of this group to coordinate development of specific, measurable indicators."

Dr Assad Hafeez, director-general of health, emphasised the importance of research in policy formation. He added that research tied to the SDGs was leading to new knowledge and was testing approaches that would lead to more effective healthcare strategies. Dr Hafeez also announced that the committee would be formed within a month and would produce annual reports to track progress on achieving the 17 inter-linked policy areas under the SDGs.

In his concluding remarks, the founding director of the Centre of Excellence in Women and Child Health at the Aga Khan University, Dr Zulfiqar A Bhutta, underscored the importance of developing appropriate indicators that would help track progress in achieving the SDGs.

"When you look at data at the national level you don't recognise the vital difference between provinces and the inequities between villages and cities in each province. Pakistan's health cannot be represented by a single set of national indicators and that is why we will assess data by district. This will enable us to create indicators relevant to our circumstances that will inform the initiatives taken by the Joint Health SDG committee."

Dr Bhutta also spoke of the need to set up an independent, representative national steering committee with links to provinces to review the pace of efforts to achieve the SDGs and to ensure that all stakeholders are held accountable.

Other prominent officials at the workshop included Federal Minister for Planning, Development and Reform Ahsan Iqbal, Minister of State for Information, Broadcasting and National Heritage Marriyum Aurangzeb and WHO Regional Convener for the Eastern Mediterranean Taskforce on SDG Dr Zafar Mirza.
